key_insight: Pairing localized textual attributes with a designer's sketch and applying multi-level conditioning enables generated fashion images that faithfully follow the sketch structure while adding fine-grained material, color, and style details.
problem_solved: Bridges the gap between sparse structural input (designer sketches) and rich semantic guidance (text) by ensuring localized textual attributes are respected spatially, preventing attribute bleeding or layout violations in fashion image generation.
method: Associate textual attribute phrases with spatial regions of the sketch (localized text–sketch pairing) so each attribute has a clear target area.
Apply multi-level conditioning (e.g., global, regional, local) during generation to enforce overall silhouette, regional consistency, and fine-grained local details.
Fuse the paired, multi-level conditioning signals into a generative pipeline to produce photorealistic fashion images that preserve sketch structure and reflect specified attributes.
impact: Provides a practical, controllable multimodal conditioning technique for fashion design tools and generative research, enabling designers and ML practitioners to produce layout-faithful and attribute-accurate images from sparse inputs.
visual_elements: Side-by-side examples: input sketch + localized text labels → generated image (before/after or multiple variants).
Diagram of pairing: sketch overlaid with colored region tags linked to short text attributes.
Multi-level conditioning flowchart: global → regional → local conditioning paths into the generator.
Attribute fidelity heatmap or attention overlay showing where each text attribute influences the output.
paper_title: Multi-Level Conditioning by Pairing Localized Text and Sketch for Fashion Image Generation
paper_authors: Ziyue Liu, Davide Talon, Federico Girella, Zanxi Ruan, Mattia Mondo
